decisions.observation: A one-millimeter normalization floor made tolerances effectively absolute for small meshes, causing scale-dependent intersection decisions. Computing (min+max)/2 could overflow for finite translated vertices.
decisions.hypothesized_cause: A one-millimeter normalization floor made tolerances effectively absolute for small meshes, causing scale-dependent intersection decisions. Computing (min+max)/2 could overflow for finite translated vertices.
decisions.change: Normalize by actual maximum mesh extent, center with half-weighted extrema, and reject zero or unrepresentable extent before geometric predicates.
decisions.predicted_consequence: Four analytically chosen intersection/nonintersection fixtures preserve their verdict from 1e-180 to 1e160; a representable mesh near 1e308 can be centered without overflow.

decisions.result: See retained verification receipt; no efficacy result is inferred.

decisions.observation: Four independent numerical/geometry candidates needed combined validation. Review found an integer-to-float conversion that reported residual zero for an integer equation whose true residual is one.
decisions.hypothesized_cause: The conversion erased integer identity before the existing floating residual calculation.
decisions.change: Merge all four histories, then inspect original integer scalars for exact float64 representation and reject lossy conversion. Preserve exactly representable large integers.
decisions.predicted_consequence: The formerly false-zero cases fail explicitly while exact large-integer controls and existing numerical/geometry behavior remain supported.
decisions.discriminating_experiment: Retained predecessor regressions, focused numerical tests and the full maintained product suite.

decisions.observation: Interval(1e-310,1e-310) divided by itself raises ValueError even though its exact quotient is one.
decisions.hypothesized_cause: Constructing the standalone reciprocal overflows before multiplication by the small numerator.
decisions.change: Round the minimum and maximum of the four direct endpoint quotients outward. Keep zero-containing divisors and nonfinite enclosure endpoints rejected.
decisions.predicted_consequence: Finite subnormal ratios enclose their exact rational results; ordinary controls and prior rejection boundaries remain valid.
decisions.discriminating_experiment: Exact-rational endpoint tests on both original and integrated parent source, plus maintained numerical tests.

limitations: Inputs whose total span is not representable in float64 are rejected explicitly.
